newsitem.title: UK: Britain comes first, Blair to tell Kok.
newsitem.headline: Britain comes first, Blair to tell Kok.

text.p: Prime Minister Tony Blair wants a new constructive partnership with Europe but will put Britain's interests "first, second and third" in next month's negotiations to reform the European Union, a senior official said on Friday.

Speaking just before Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok arrived for talks, the official said Blair was determined to draw a line under the "ridiculous ideological hatreds" that he said marked the previous Conservative government's dealings with Europe.
The new Labour government, elected last week with a landslide majority that ended 18 years of Conservative rule, intended to show positive and constructive leadership.
But Blair would tell Kok, who will chair next month's summit in Amsterdam on how to overhaul the EU's workings, that his sole negotiating yardstick would be the British national interest.
Blair took a tough line on Europe in the heat of the election campaign, promising to stick up for Britain at the Amsterdam summit, and his officials said he meant it.
"The noises made during the election were real and not put on for the electorate," one said.

Specifically, Blair will tell Kok there is no question of Britain's agreeing to hand over control of its borders to the EU, and it will demand an opt-out from any Amsterdam treaty deal on the subject.

Similarly, Britain has no intention of surrendering control of foreign policy or of agreeing to Franco-German proposals for the Western European Union, a defence alliance, to be integrated into the EU, officials said.
But Blair planned to tell Kok that Britain was committed to reaching a deal at Amsterdam, which officials in Brussels say is vital to plans to expand the bloc to take in former communist countries.

The negotiations would be tough, but Blair would approach them as a dialogue, not as a war. He would press Britain's priorities of completing the EU single market, reforming its common agricultural policy, enlargement and measures to improve labour market flexibility, the officials said.
